source_refs.note: Topic 5.2.3 with 5.2.3.2 Standard Deviation and the class activity (PDF 129-132, printed 126-129). The formulas print garbled; Class B's root prints '456' and SD 21.26 (correct 454 and 21.31); Class A's SD 3.55 is 3.54. Recorded.

blocks.text: Measures of dispersion tell how spread out the data are. Variance is the average squared distance of the values from the mean: variance = (1/N) x sum of (xi - mean)^2, where xi is each value, the mean is written mu and N is the number of values. Standard deviation is the square root of the variance, in the same units as the data.

blocks.caption: Two classes on the same exam

blocks.text: Class A: mean 274 / 5 = 54.8, variance 62.8 / 5 = 12.56, standard deviation about 3.54. Class B: mean 295 / 5 = 59, variance 2270 / 5 = 454, standard deviation about 21.31. Class B's scores are far more spread out, while Class A's are packed closely around the mean.

blocks.alt: Top left: dot plots of Class A scores 50 to 60 and Class B scores 30 to 90 with mean lines and shaded one-standard-deviation bands. Top right: three boxes for survey, observation and experiment with examples. Bottom: a grade table with the misspelt name Alie and a missing grade for Sara, an arrow, and the cleaned table with Ali and 75, plus notes on imputation, flagging and removal.
blocks.caption: Spread of data, collection methods and data cleaning (original diagram after topics 5.2 and 5.3).
blocks.long_description: Class A's five scores sit close together around a mean of 54.8, with standard deviation 3.54, while Class B's scores spread from 30 to 90 around a mean of 59, with standard deviation 21.31, so the same average can hide very different spreads. Data can be collected by surveys that ask set questions, observations that watch without interfering, or experiments that change one variable. Cleaning corrects the misspelt name Alie to Ali and fills Sara's missing grade, here with 75; a missing value can also be imputed from an average, flagged, or left out of an analysis.

blocks.prompt: Class activity: for the homework hours 3, 5, 8, 8, 10, 12, 15, 15, 16, 18, find the mean, median, mode, variance and standard deviation.
blocks.explanation: Mean 110 / 10 = 11; median (10 + 12) / 2 = 11; modes 8 and 15; squared deviations 64, 36, 9, 9, 1, 1, 16, 16, 25, 49 add to 226, so variance 22.6 and standard deviation about 4.75. Most students do about 11 hours, but habits vary by roughly 5 hours either way.

items: Variance: mean of squared deviations; SD: its square root. Class A 12.56 and 3.54; Class B 454 and 21.31.
